subject: math
cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
skillName: Build new functions from existing functions
intro: End-of-cluster mastery check for Building Functions, cluster B: Build new functions from existing functions. Twelve multiple-choice items spanning both standards in the cluster: transformations of functions ($A2.F\text{-}BF.B.3$) and inverse functions ($A2.F\text{-}BF.B.4$). Items are grouped by standard.

items.prompt:
Describe how the graph of $g(x)=f(x)+6$ compares to the graph of $f(x)$.
A) A vertical shift up $6$ units
B) A vertical shift down $6$ units
C) A horizontal shift right $6$ units
D) A horizontal shift left $6$ units
items.answer: A) A vertical shift up $6$ units

steps: Adding a constant $k$ outside the function, $f(x)+k$, moves the graph vertically by $k$ units.
Here $k=+6$, so the graph shifts up $6$ units.
B reverses the direction of the shift. C and D treat an outside change as horizontal, but a change outside the function is vertical.
solution.answer: A) A vertical shift up $6$ units

items.prompt:
Describe how the graph of $g(x)=4f(x)$ compares to the graph of $f(x)$.
A) A vertical compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{4}$
B) A vertical stretch by a factor of $4$
C) A horizontal stretch by a factor of $4$
D) A vertical shift up $4$ units
items.answer: B) A vertical stretch by a factor of $4$

steps: Multiplying the whole function by $k$, $kf(x)$, scales the outputs by $|k|$.
Since $|k|=4>1$, the outputs grow, which is a vertical stretch by a factor of $4$.
A reverses stretch and compression. C treats an outside multiplier as a horizontal change. D treats a multiplier as a shift.
solution.answer: B) A vertical stretch by a factor of $4$

items.prompt:
Describe how the graph of $g(x)=f(x-3)$ compares to the graph of $f(x)$.
A) A horizontal shift left $3$ units
B) A horizontal shift right $3$ units
C) A vertical shift down $3$ units
D) A vertical shift up $3$ units
items.answer: B) A horizontal shift right $3$ units

steps: A change inside the function, $f(x+k)$, shifts the graph horizontally in the direction opposite the sign of $k$.
Here the input is $x-3$, so $k=-3$ and the graph moves right $3$ units.
A reverses the counterintuitive direction. C and D treat an inside change as a vertical shift.
solution.answer: B) A horizontal shift right $3$ units

items.prompt:
Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$. Which equation represents the graph of $f$ shifted left $2$ units and down $1$ unit?
A) $g(x)=\sqrt{x-2}+1$
B) $g(x)=\sqrt{x+2}-1$
C) $g(x)=\sqrt{x-2}-1$
D) $g(x)=\sqrt{x+2}+1$

steps: A shift left $2$ replaces $x$ with $x+2$, giving $\sqrt{x+2}$.
A shift down $1$ subtracts $1$ outside, giving $\sqrt{x+2}-1$.
A and C use $x-2$, which shifts right, not left. D adds $1$ outside, which shifts up, not down.

items.prompt:
Starting from $f(x)=x^{2}$, apply a vertical stretch by a factor of $3$, a reflection across the $x$-axis, and a shift right $1$ unit and up $4$ units. Which equation is $g(x)$?
A) $g(x)=3(x-1)^{2}+4$
B) $g(x)=-3(x+1)^{2}+4$
C) $g(x)=-3(x-1)^{2}+4$
D) $g(x)=-3(x-1)^{2}-4$

steps: The vertical stretch by $3$ and reflection across the $x$-axis give the coefficient $-3$, producing $-3f(x)$.
A shift right $1$ replaces $x$ with $x-1$, and a shift up $4$ adds $4$ outside: $g(x)=-3(x-1)^{2}+4$.
A drops the reflection, so its leading coefficient is positive. B uses $x+1$, which shifts left instead of right. D subtracts $4$, shifting down instead of up.

items.prompt:
Describe the transformation of $f(x)$ given by $g(x)=f(2x-6)$.
A) A horizontal compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ and a shift right $3$ units
B) A horizontal compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ and a shift right $6$ units
C) A horizontal stretch by a factor of $2$ and a shift right $3$ units
D) A horizontal compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ and a shift left $3$ units
items.answer: A) A horizontal compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ and a shift right $3$ units

steps: Factor the input to read the shift correctly: $f(2x-6)=f\big(2(x-3)\big)$.
The factor $2$ inside gives a horizontal compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}$, and the $x-3$ gives a shift right $3$ units.
B reads the shift as $6$ without factoring out the $2$. C reverses compression and stretch. D reverses the direction of the horizontal shift.
solution.answer: A) A horizontal compression by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ and a shift right $3$ units

steps: Write $y=3x-7$, then solve for $x$: add $7$ to get $y+7=3x$, then divide by $3$ to get $x=\frac{y+7}{3}$.
Swap the variables: $f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x+7}{3}$.
B divides before adding, reversing the order of operations. C is the reciprocal, not the inverse function. D negates each term instead of inverting the operations.
Since $f(a)=b$ means $f^{-1}(b)=a$, find the input $a$ with $f(a)=11$: solve $2a+5=11$.
Subtract $5$ to get $2a=6$, then divide by $2$ to get $a=3$, so $f^{-1}(11)=3$.
A evaluates the original function $f(11)=2(11)+5=27$ instead of the inverse. C subtracts $5$ but forgets to divide. D takes a reciprocal.
The inverse swaps inputs and outputs: $f^{-1}(9)$ is the input whose output is $9$.
A returns the output $9$ maps from itself incorrectly by reading the wrong column. C uses the input paired with $16$, not $9$. D takes a reciprocal.

items.prompt:
Find the inverse of $f(x)=\sqrt{x-2}$ for $x\ge 2$.
A) $f^{-1}(x)=x^{2}-2$ for $x\ge 0$
B) $f^{-1}(x)=x^{2}+2$ for $x\ge 0$
C) $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x+2}$ for $x\ge -2$
D) $f^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x-2}}$

steps: Write $y=\sqrt{x-2}$ and solve for $x$: square both sides to get $y^{2}=x-2$, then add $2$ to get $x=y^{2}+2$.
Swap the variables: $f^{-1}(x)=x^{2}+2$. The range of $f$ is $y\ge 0$, so the domain of $f^{-1}$ is $x\ge 0$.
A squares only one piece, dropping the $+2$ correction. C never squares to undo the radical. D is the reciprocal, not the inverse.
Write $y=\frac{x+3}{x-2}$ and multiply both sides by $x-2$: $y(x-2)=x+3$, so $xy-2y=x+3$.
Collect the $x$ terms: $xy-x=2y+3$, factor to get $x(y-1)=2y+3$, so $x=\frac{2y+3}{y-1}$.
Swap the variables: $f^{-1}(x)=\frac{2x+3}{x-1}$.
A just inverts the fraction (the reciprocal), not the function. C has the wrong signs from a collection error. D negates terms instead of solving.

items.prompt:
Does $f(x)=x^{2}$ defined on all real numbers have an inverse function, and why?
A) Yes, because every quadratic function has an inverse function
B) Yes, its inverse is $f^{-1}(x)=\pm\sqrt{x}$
C) No, because it fails the horizontal line test; an inverse exists only if the domain is restricted, for example to $x\ge 0$
D) No, because squaring can never be undone
items.answer: C) No, because it fails the horizontal line test; an inverse exists only if the domain is restricted, for example to $x\ge 0$

steps: An inverse function exists only when $f$ is one-to-one, which it must pass the horizontal line test to be.

On all real numbers $f(x)=x^{2}$ is not one-to-one, since $f(2)=f(-2)=4$, so a horizontal line meets the graph twice and no inverse function exists unless the domain is restricted, for example to $x\ge 0$.
A is false because not every quadratic is one-to-one. B is not a function because it assigns two outputs to one input. D is wrong because squaring can be undone once the domain is restricted.
solution.answer: C) No, because it fails the horizontal line test; an inverse exists only if the domain is restricted, for example to $x\ge 0$
